text:
maria: Heads-up — customer on-prem VPC started seeing job failures after last week's kernel security patch. Symptoms: NCCL init errors and GPU driver OOMs. Attaching small log snippet below.

jake: Which customer / cluster? can you paste nvidia-smi + uname -r and the cuda version from the env? :eyes:

maria: customer: ACME-Health, cluster: onprem-eu-01.
```
> nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name --format=csv
Driver Version, GPU Name
515.86.01, A100-SXM4-80GB
```
```
> uname -r
4.18.0-425.el8.x86_64
```
And container CUDA: 11.8. NCCL errors: "NCCL error in: unhandled system error" during all-reduce.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-4321 (priority: P2) — assigned to eng-infra.

alex: This looks like driver/user-space drift. Many distros backport kernel patches without rebuilding nvidia modules; 515 + kernel combos can break NCCL with CUDA 11.8. Our private matrix lists 520+ as recommended for NCCL v2.14, but we still have customers on 515.

ryan: Sales says ACME refused kernel rollback due to compliance. They patched to 4.18.0-425 and want to keep it. Theyre asking if we can support a vendor-provided kernel patch instead of rolling back.

jake: Short-term: collect full dmesg and module log. Long-term: we need a policy for private installs. Proposal: host preflight that asserts (driver_major, driver_minor, kernel_range) and refuses to register the node if out-of-matrix unless an override token is provided.

maria: dmesg shows tainted modules and binder errors referencing nvidia. Repro: run multi-GPU allreduce, NCCL stalls after 2-3 iterations.

alex: Agree on preflight. Also, add a recommended action set: (A) rebuild kernel modules via DKMS on the host, (B) provide a signed backported driver bundle we can ship for RHEL8, (C) offer a temporary fallback to CPU-only NOK. For Private customers we should require a "driver-lock" entry in the deployment manifest listing allowed driver ranges.

customer-eng: ACME asked about extra cost for driver rebuild + validation. Rough estimate from support: 4-8 engineer hours + 2 hours on-call for rollout, plus one canary host. Charging for ad-hoc on-prem work seems reasonable.

jake: Documenting supported matrix is urgent. Also add a checklist for troubleshooting: grep for "NCCL INFO" and "CUDA_ERROR" in worker logs; check "modinfo nvidia" and verify kernel-compat. Example commands to add to docs:
```
sudo modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic
sudo dkms status
journalctl -u kubelet | grep nvidia
```

maria: I will prepare a small support package for ACME: 1) host preflight script, 2) DKMS rebuild instructions, 3) a signed driver blob we can test on a canary host. Tagging @sre-rotations for weekend window.

sre-rotations: Can take the canary on Saturday morning. Need the canary host names and a rollback playbook.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary package "onprem-driver-fix-2025-05-04" deployed to onprem-canary group (3 nodes) — status: in-progress.

alex: After canary we should update the private deployment docs and add the driver-lock requirement to the next minor release. Also add a note in pricing: emergency on-prem driver rebuilds billable.

ryan: Well brief ACME tomorrow and offer 2 options: let us deliver the rebuilt driver + validation (billable) or we give them a prescriptive rollback. They prefer us to handle it.

maria: Plan: run canary Friday night, validate NCCL allreduce at scale, if green schedule Saturday patch. Ill open a PR for the preflight script and a short KB for support.

jake: Also file a follow-up to add kernel-driver compatibility to the Redwood Optimize insights so we can proactively flag customers with risky combos.

customer-eng: FYI, ACME also asked whether wed add this to the "supported matrix" public doc. They want clarity before committing to a maintenance window.

alex: We should publish a private matrix for enterprise/procurement and a public guidance doc that lists recommended driver ranges. Avoid promising support for every distro-patched kernel.

maria: OK — Ill draft the private matrix update and tag @ryan and @alex for sign-off. :thumbsup:

jake: thanks all. short-term ticket created: INFRA-2142 to track preflight + driver bundle.

maria: closing loop here, will update thread with canary results. :wave:
